text:
Alex C.: Heads up — saw a big coldstart spike for inference in eu-west-1 this morning, p95 ~2.3x normal. Warm pool for gpu-eu-warm had TTL expire ~30m before spike.
Priya Nair: digging in logs, scale-to-zero triggered for gpu-eu-warm because queue length dropped. Several spot nodes reclaimed in eu-west-1c right before the surge.
Jonathon K.: we intentionally set short TTLs in EU to save cost — IIRC it was 15m. EU AZs have slower boot times than us-west which makes this more visible.
Sarah L.: Were customers impacted or did fallback behavior cover it?
Alex C.: some requests hit the fallback smaller model for ~3m until the nodes came up. Not a total outage, but SLA p95 got clipped for two routes.
autoscaler-bot: Cluster-autoscaler: scale-up requested 4 nodes for gpu-eu-warm. Provisioning failed in eu-west-1a: insufficient capacity; 2 nodes provisioned, 2 pending.
Priya Nair: quick proposal — increase warm-pool TTL for eu-west to 1h, add shutdown-jitter to avoid mass expiry, and reserve 1 on-demand GPU per AZ as insurance. Also label warm-pool nodes with route-group=inference-host so prewarming targets the right workload.
Jonathon K.: +1 on jitter. We should avoid single TTL for all regions — EU needs longer defaults. Also consider a light-weight keepalive: keep one tiny on-demand instance that can accept traffic and prime KV caches.
Sarah L.: what's the estimated cost delta for keeping 1 on-demand GPU per AZ in eu-west?
Priya Nair: rough calc: +~$12k/month for minimal reserve across eu-west, assuming current on-demand rates and 3 AZs. That offsets repeat SLA penalty exposure we saw (estimated ~ $25k per incident window historically).
Alex C.: implementation steps I'm proposing: bump `warmPool.ttlSeconds` to 3600 for eu-west config, set `warmPool.shutdownJitterSeconds` to 300, and set `warmPool.reserveOnDemandPerAZ` = 1. We'll canary in eu-west-1 and monitor.
Priya Nair: config snippet I'll push in helm values:
```
warmPool:
  ttlSeconds: 3600
  shutdownJitterSeconds: 300
  reserveOnDemandPerAZ: 1
```
Jonathon K.: long-term we should make TTL dynamic per workload based on request inter-arrival histogram and queue length. Add as RFC for Q2.
Priya Nair: for now I'll open PR and run canary rollout for 24h. Will add dashboards: warm-pool-expiry, podReadyLatency, p95-inference-latency per-route.
Alex C.: @Sarah L can you sign off on the spend delta so we can do the canary today?
Sarah L.: sign-off for canary. Keep an eye on cost alert thresholds.
Alex C.: thanks — scheduling a 30m deploy window today at 16:00 UTC. I'll post updates in this thread when the rollout completes and attach Prom graphs.
Priya Nair: will also add a small metric to emit when warm-pool evictions are due to spot reclaim vs controller TTL, so we can differentiate causes.
Jonathon K.: small nit — add a randomized backoff when recreating K8s nodepool to avoid AWS API rate bursts across AZs.
Alex C.: noted. Thanks all.
